68 matched pool-focused rows; pooling-disabled controls omitted. Linux SQL/hold median 1.004x (29/35 within 0.9x-1.1x); Windows 1.075x (18/35).
Speedup is calculated within each platform: legacy mean / new-pool mean. 1.0x is parity.
SQL/hold-heavy = executes SQL commands or deliberately holds a checked-out connection; pool overhead is only part of the measured time.
Notes on platform-specific timing regressions greater than 1.1x slower
1. Linux: async single-thread churn at depths 10 and 100 exposes reuse order: the legacy LIFO stack reuses one hot connection; the FIFO channel rotates through the idle set, reducing locality.
2. Linux: multi-command reuse (P=10, Pool=50) checks out once, then runs 5-15 SQL commands. SQL/server time dominates; the regression reproduced in 2 of 3 runs.
3. Linux: with 4 minimum worker threads, 50 sync callers competing for 10 connections starve queued channel continuations. Results return near parity at worker floors 16, 32, and 128.
4. Windows: sync single-thread churn at depths 100 exposes reuse order: the legacy LIFO stack reuses one hot connection; the FIFO channel rotates through the idle set, reducing locality.
5. Windows: bursty traffic (P=50, Pool=100) runs 1-5 SQL queries per checkout in waves. SQL/server variance dominates; the slowdown appeared in 1 of 3 runs.
6. Windows: with 4 and 128 minimum worker threads, 50 sync callers competing for 10 connections starve queued channel continuations. Results return near parity at worker floors 16 and 32.
